title: Ohtani Set for Dodgers' Game 3 NLCS Lineup, Confirms Roberts – ESPN Report
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed on Tuesday that two‑time National League MVP Shohei Ohtani will take the field in Game 3 of the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers, despite a recent slump that has raised questions about his health and effectiveness. Roberts said he had a “great conversation” with Ohtani, who expressed confidence that he is on the verge of a turnaround and eager to contribute in the pivotal matchup slated for Wednesday night.  

Ohtani’s recent performance has been a stark contrast to the dominant start he gave the Dodgers in the early weeks of the season. After a blistering stretch that saw him hit .380 with 12 home runs and pitch a sub‑2.00 ERA, the Japanese star has seen his batting average dip below .200 and his fastball velocity dip a few miles per hour. The slump has been attributed to a lingering shoulder irritation, minor fatigue from a heavy workload, and the mental pressure of carrying a dual‑role on a team that has already clinched the NL West. Nevertheless, the 30‑year‑old remains one of the most valuable assets in baseball, and his presence in the lineup is expected to shift the strategic calculus for both clubs.  

Roberts’ decision to keep Ohtani in the roster reflects a broader trend in the Dodgers’ postseason strategy: trusting veteran talent while managing risk. The Dodgers have already leaned on their deep bench, rotating relievers, and a versatile bench to mitigate the impact of any single player’s dip. In the bullpen, closer Blake Treinen and setup man Blake Snell have been reliable, while the offense has been buoyed by contributions from Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts and newly acquired outfielder Cody Bellinger. By confirming Ohtani’s availability, Roberts signals that the team believes the potential upside outweighs the lingering concerns, especially given the Brewers’ potent lineup featuring William Contreras, Willy Adames and a rejuvenated Christian Yelich.  

From a tactical standpoint, Ohtani’s role could be multifaceted. If he returns to his usual 2‑3‑5 split—starting on the mound and then taking a spot in the batting order—Los Angeles gains a rare tactical advantage that forces Milwaukee to juggle its pitching staff. Even a limited pinch‑hit or defensive appearance would force the Brewers to adjust their bullpen usage. Moreover, Ohanami’s presence may provide a psychological boost to the Dodgers’ younger players, who have watched his meteoric rise and now look to him for leadership as the series reaches its midpoint.  

The Brewers, meanwhile, are likely to exploit Ohtani’s recent struggles, targeting him with aggressive pitching sequences and defensive shifts designed to limit his power. Milwaukee’s ace, Corbin Burnes, has shown an ability to dominate even elite hitters, and the Brewers’ bullpen depth could be a decisive factor if Ohtani’s slump persists. However, history shows that Ohtani thrives under pressure; his postseason résumé includes a clutch home run in the 2022 World Series and a dominant start in the 2023 NLDS. If he can recapture even a fraction of his early‑season form, the Dodgers will have a decisive edge in a series that is currently tied 1‑1.  

Looking ahead, Game 3 will likely serve as a litmus test for Ohanami’s postseason trajectory. A strong showing could reignite his season and propel Los Angeles toward a third straight World Series appearance, while continued struggles could force the Dodgers to lean even more heavily on their depth and perhaps reconsider Ohanami’s dual‑role usage in later games. As the NLCS shifts to Milwaukee for Games 4 and 5, the Dodgers will need to balance the desire to maximize Ohanami’s impact with the practicalities of health and stamina. For now, fans and analysts alike will be watching closely as one of baseball’s most electrifying talents steps back onto the field, hoping that the “great conversation” with Roberts translates into a decisive performance that tilts the series in Los Angeles’ favor.
